evidence.claim: In the conventional (one-step) process the CO2 single-pass conversion is 28.5 %, against an equilibrium conversion of 30.4 %; the three-step process with intermediate condensation reaches 53.9 %.
limits: Aspen Plus V10 simulation, not measured.

evidence.claim: The reactor runs at 70 bar; each module has 33,000 tubes of 12.5 m length and 3.75 cm inner diameter.
limits: Six modules in the one-step process (supplement p. 9).

evidence.claim: One-step flowsheet: effluent cooled to 30 C, high-pressure flash with a purged and recompressed gas recycle, liquid let down to 1 bar and flashed at 30 C with a purged gas recycle to the CO2 feed, packed column giving methanol (>99.5 % m/m) as liquid distillate, water as bottoms and CO2 in a gas distillate.
limits: Process description; numbers are in the supplement.

evidence.claim: Peng-Robinson is used in the reactor modules and NRTL with its second binary set (NRTL2) in all other equipment.
limits: Parameters not printed (Aspen databank).

evidence.claim: The column has 30 stages, feed above stage 24, reflux ratio 2, a kettle reboiler and a partial condenser at 53 C with liquid and vapour distillates; water leaves at 99.99 % and methanol at 99.67 % mol/mol.
limits: Murphree efficiency 0.75 on intermediate stages in the paper; the reflux ratio's basis (whole or liquid distillate) is not printed.

evidence.claim: FLASH3 runs at 30 C and 69.25 bar; its liquid (stream 24) still holds a considerable amount of CO2, 18.545 mol % in Table S10.
limits: Aspen Plus with NRTL2, parameters not printed.

evidence.claim: 2 % of the high-pressure flash gas (44-PURGE, 1051 kmol/h) and 2 % of the low-pressure flash gas (45-PURGE, 51 kmol/h) are purged; the rest is recycled.
limits: Purges burned in a fired heater, outside Lab's model.

evidence.claim: Table S10: 30-WATER 99.985 mol % water; 31-MEOH 99.667 mol % methanol, 0.316 % CO2; gas distillate 32 36.909 % CO2, 62.974 % methanol.
limits: Aspen Plus simulation.

evidence.claim: Table S14 gives the cooling-water exchanger HE7 24.2 MW; the case's audit derives 19.75 MW from the printed enthalpies of streams 22 and 23 (Table S9).
limits: The 19.75 MW is Lab's derived value (cases/methanol-co2-campos-2022/STREAM_AUDIT.md), not printed by the authors.

evidence.claim: Table S10: the FLASH4 liquid 28 (the column feed) holds 1.285 mol % CO2, 50.041 % methanol, 48.671 % water.
limits: Aspen Plus simulation.

plain.title: CO2 hydrogenation to methanol: boiling-water-cooled multitubular reactors at 70 bar with gas recycle
plain.when: CO2 and H2 react to methanol and water, exothermic and limited by equilibrium.
plain.do: Use parallel modules of 33,000 tubes (12.5 m, 3.75 cm), Cu/ZnO/Al2O3, at 70 bar, cooled by boiling water (Campos et al. 2022), and recycle the unconverted gas.
plain.why: High pressure favours methanol; boiling water holds the tubes near isothermal.
plain.check: Single-pass CO2 conversion 28.5 % against 30.4 % at equilibrium (Campos et al. 2022, abstract).

decisions.obstacle: Methanol synthesis from CO2 is exothermic and equilibrium-limited; one pass converts little CO2.
decisions.mechanism: High pressure favours methanol; tubes cooled by boiling water hold the reactor near isothermal; the unconverted gas is recycled.
decisions.operation: Six parallel modules of 33,000 tubes (12.5 m, 3.75 cm), Cu/ZnO/Al2O3, 70 bar, boiling water on the shell.
decisions.expected_change: Single-pass CO2 conversion near equilibrium (28.5 % against 30.4 %).
alternatives: Three-step process with two intermediate condensations (53.9 % per pass; same paper)
limits: Higher pressures were left out by the authors (kinetic extrapolation, condensation in the reactor, compression cost; article p. 4).
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

plain.title: Release the dissolved gases in two flashes, 70 bar then 1 bar, and recycle the low-pressure CO2
plain.when: The condensate of the 70 bar loop holds dissolved CO2 and light gases.
plain.do: Flash at 30 C and 69.25 bar, let the liquid down to 1 bar and flash at 30 C again; recycle that gas to the CO2 feed less a 2 % purge (Campos et al. 2022).
plain.why: Keeps the gases out of the methanol column.
plain.check: The column feed should hold about 1.285 mol % CO2.

decisions.obstacle: The condensate of the 70 bar loop holds dissolved CO2 and light gases that must not reach the product column.
decisions.mechanism: Separate the light gases at high pressure, then release most remaining CO2 by letdown to 1 bar, and recycle it to the CO2 feed.
decisions.operation: FLASH3 at 30 C, 69.25 bar; valve to 1 bar; FLASH4 at 30 C; FLASH4 gas (less 2 %) mixed with the column's gas distillate and the CO2 feed.
decisions.expected_change: Column feed nearly free of gases (1.285 mol % CO2 in stream 28).
limits: The paper's own simulated design (Aspen Plus V10, NRTL2).
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

plain.title: Methanol-water column with dissolved CO2: partial condenser with a gas and a liquid distillate
plain.when: The column feed still holds CO2 and traces of H2, CO and N2.
plain.do: Use 30 stages, feed above stage 24, reflux ratio 2, and a partial condenser at 53 C with liquid and vapour distillates (Campos et al. 2022).
plain.why: The gases leave in the vapour distillate and methanol as liquid.

decisions.obstacle: The column feed still holds CO2 and traces of H2, CO and N2 that a total condenser could not keep out of the methanol.
decisions.mechanism: A partial condenser at 53 C sends the gases to a vapour distillate while methanol leaves as liquid distillate.
decisions.operation: 30 stages, feed above stage 24, reflux ratio 2, condenser 53 C with liquid and vapour distillates, kettle reboiler.
limits: The paper's own simulated design.
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

plain.title: Purge 2 % of each flash gas to bound the inerts in the recycle
plain.when: N2, CO and excess H2 build up in the gas recycle.
plain.do: Purge 2 % of the high-pressure and 2 % of the low-pressure flash gas, recycle the rest, and burn the purges (Campos et al. 2022).
plain.why: A fixed purge fraction bounds the inert inventory.

decisions.obstacle: N2, CO and excess H2 build up in the gas recycle.
decisions.mechanism: Purge a fixed fraction of each flash gas; recycle the rest.
decisions.operation: 2 % of the high-pressure flash gas and 2 % of the low-pressure flash gas purged and burned.
decisions.expected_change: Bounded inert inventory; recycle about 2.7 times the fresh gas.
limits: The purge fraction was chosen in the paper's own optimisation (0.5-5 % studied, article Section 2.4); not reproduced by Lab.
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.

plain.title: Cool the reactor effluent through three feed-effluent exchangers before cooling water
plain.when: The reactor effluent near 248 C must be cooled to 30 C while three cold streams need heat.
plain.do: Heat the reactor feed, the column feed and the low-pressure flash feed with the effluent, then cool the rest with water (Campos et al. 2022).
plain.why: Recovers the reaction heat inside the plant.
plain.check: The cooling-water duty of Table S14 (24.2 MW) and the stream enthalpies disagree; see the cooler lesson.

decisions.obstacle: The reactor effluent at about 248 C must be cooled to 30 C while three cold streams need heat.
decisions.mechanism: Feed-effluent exchangers recover the heat before cooling water takes the rest.
decisions.operation: HE4 heats the reactor feed, HE5 the column feed, HE6 the low-pressure flash feed; HE7 with cooling water to 30 C.
limits: The paper's own design; Table S14 and the stream enthalpies disagree on HE7 (24.2 against 19.75 MW, derived).
Draft, written by an AI session from the case files (2026-11-20); not reviewed.
